item.title: CLARA Launches Agentic Claims Platform
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) CLARA Analytics (Sunnyvale, Calif.) has launched Agentic Intelligence, an AI workforce built into the company’s CLARAty.ai platform for complex casualty and workers’ compensation claims. “We built Agentic Intelligence to give adjusters a partner that reviews claims data and documents to surface real-time changes in severity, litigation potential, fraud risk and closure opportunities.” Wilson says the platform is intended to move CLARA from a system of intelligence to a system of action, with agents synthesizing claim information, providing transparent reasoning and surfacing opportunities for action. Agentic Claims Intelligence Agentic Intelligence gives adjusters access to information on where a score came from and how current the underlying data is, according to CLARA.

item.title: Head of Environmental Firm Sentenced to Prison for Asbestos Left at Chicago Worksite
item.description: A federal judge has sentenced the president of an environmental services company to more than six and a half years in federal prison for knowingly leaving asbestos at a suburban Chicago demolition site after accepting full payment for the purported remediation, according to a press release by the U.S. Carl Fioravanti was the president of Alliance Environmental Control, Inc., a Lansing, Ill.-based company that performs asbestos removal services. Two months after Fioravanti certified the project as fully remediated, the property owner learned that Alliance had left enormous amounts of asbestos-containing materials throughout portions of the site.

item.title: Cyber Threats the Top Business Concern as AI Heightens Risk: Travelers Risk Index
item.description: According to the latest Risk Index from insurer Travelers, 58% of respondents said they worry a great deal or some about cyber risks. Cyber threats ranked as the top overall business concern for the fifth time in eight years. “Businesses view cyber threats as a serious concern, and they’re getting smarter and more prepared – investing in controls, building confidence and turning to their insurance carrier for guidance,” said John Menefee, vice president and enterprise cyber lead at Travelers.

item.title: Reinsurance access remains critical to Florida market’s stability, says Morningstar DBRS
item.description: A new report from Morningstar DBRS has suggested that, given Florida’s significant hurricane exposure, continued access to “affordable and readily available” reinsurance will remain critical to the market’s long-term stability and financial strength. “Given Florida’s significant hurricane exposure, continued access to affordable and readily available reinsurance will remain critical to the market’s long-term stability and financial strength.” Elsewhere in the report, Morningstar DBRS also noted that the remainder of the 2026 hurricane season will still be an important test of recent market improvements. According to Morningstar DBRS, that period was marked by numerous insurer insolvencies, rising reinsurance costs, excessive litigation, and a contraction in private insurance market capacity.

item.title: Arcadian Risk Capital appoints Matthew Mullen to lead US Enterprise Casualty expansion
item.description: Arcadian Risk Capital, a specialty managing general agent (MGA) operating across Bermuda, Ireland, the UK and the US, has appointed Matthew Mullen as Executive Vice President as the company establishes a new presence in the US Enterprise Casualty market. Mullen, who will be based in New York, has been appointed to oversee the development of Arcadian’s Enterprise risk offering. The investment followed Arcadian’s expansion across its existing markets and provides additional backing as the company develops new lines of specialty insurance business, including its Enterprise Casualty operation in the US.

item.title: Holistic, enduring partnerships key as reinsurance capital grows: Hannover Re’s Althoff
item.description: As reinsurance capital is more abundant and client needs become increasingly complex, cedents are looking for holistic, enduring partnerships built on predictability and aligned profitability, Sven Althoff, Member of the Executive Board for Property & Casualty at Hannover Re, noted during Aon’s latest Capital Outlook panel. I’m completely with that statement, and from that point of view, it’s really the depth and the broadness of the relationships.” Althoff shared his view of capital as a means rather than the end with Aeolus’ Dutt, who also argued that the real differentiator in reinsurance is the advisory and structural expertise applied to complex balance sheet challenges. Anshuman Srivastava, Global Chief Broking Officer at Aon, questioned a panel of experts, including Althoff, Aditya Dutt, Partner and President at ILS fund Aeolus Capital Management, and Eveline Takken-Somers, Head of Insurance Linked Investments at PGGM, to explore how capital can deliver true value today, beyond simply providing capacity.

item.title: Markets/Coverages: Munich Re Specialty Launches in Italy’s Primary Specialty Market
item.description: Munich Re Specialty announced it will offer commercial solutions in the Italian primary specialty insurance market, with its Italian headquarters in Milan. Munich Re Specialty intends to provide solutions to a range of clients from small-to-medium-sized enterprises, mid-market and upper mid-market clients in Italy, with first risks insured in early 2027. Building on its long-standing presence in the UK and Ireland and following the commencement of its operations in the Spanish and German primary specialty mid-market, this announcement marks the next stage of Munich Re Specialty’s European strategy.

item.title: Florida Farm Manager the Latest to Plead Guilty in Crop Insurance Fraud Probe
item.description: A southwest Florida farm manager could soon face years in prison and more than $3 million in restitution after he pleaded guilty to crop insurance fraud at one of Florida’s highest-profile farm operations. Mark Frisbie, 60, of Punta Gorda, pleaded guilty to one count of making a false statement in a federal crop insurance claim and greatly underreporting production and sales from bell pepper crops at farms around Immokalee, near Fort Myers, federal court records show. The plan swindled $1.7 million from the Federal Crop Insurance Corp.

In an emailed statement the FBI said it “is aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov , a bureau career website, and is currently investigating.” Fbijobs.gov on Sept. On Wednesday morning, the FBI emailed all personnel saying it was investigating the hackers’ allegations, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: VIG acquires 25% stake in Dolphin Technologies
item.description: Vienna Insurance Group (VIG) has acquired a 25% stake in Vienna-based technology company Dolphin Technologies, with the relevant agreements now signed. Founded in Vienna in 2001, Dolphin Technologies develops AI-powered telematics platforms and digital mobility services for insurance and automotive companies. Harald Trautsch, founder and chief executive officer of Dolphin Technologies, said the investment marked a logical next step.

item.title: U.S. Issues Short-term Waiver on Working Hours for Fuel Truck Drivers
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Wednesday the Trump administration is temporarily relaxing rules on hours of service by truck drivers handling gasoline and diesel, citing supply and cost concerns. The 90-day waiver took effect on September 16, 2026, allowing drivers to operate up to 16 hours within a 24-hour window, versus 14 under existing rules, so long as they take required rest breaks. Duffy said the waiver was because short-term supply chain disruptions could delay gasoline and diesel shipments, which could affect freight deliveries.

item.title: State of Emergency Declared in California in Anticipation of More El Niño-driven Storms
item.description: On Monday, California Governor Newsom issued a state of emergency proclamation, mobilizing state resources ahead of potential winter storms and other impacts. The emergency proclamation mobilizes state resources and streamlines procurement to prepare for El Niño’s anticipated impacts, like strong storms and coastal flooding. For California, the strong storms generated could lead to repeated rounds of heavy rain, strong winds, mountain snow, flooding, landslides, debris flows, large waves, and coastal flooding, especially when storms hit during very high tides.

item.title: Viewpoint: Surplus Lines Insurers Offer Vital Cover for Growing Tech-Driven Industries
item.description: As technological advancements become more ingrained in the development of entirely new industries and change the nature of existing industries, accessing needed coverage for complex risks through surplus lines carriers will become more of the path to success. Coverages for many complex exposures, especially newer ones, are not readily available through standard market insurers, elevating the need for the specialized coverage solutions that are prevalent in the surplus lines market. Surplus lines insurers have always remained ready, flexible and innovative amid market shifts and emerging exposures.

item.title: The Emerging M&A Map For AI Agent Security
item.description: Cybersecurity platforms, cloud companies and enterprise software vendors may eventually need agent-security capabilities embedded directly into their products. That creates enormous productivity potential, but it also creates a new security problem: Companies now need to protect not only users, devices and applications, but software actors that can take actions on their behalf. An agent may access corporate files, query databases, send emails or execute code.

item.title: New Jersey Fines Data Center $1 Million Over Generators It Says Were Not Permitted
item.description: The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) announced that it is ordering a $1.07 million fine against the DataOne data center in Vineland for allegedly installing and operating 62 large natural-gas power generators without the requisite state permits. DEP claims the data center has violated the New Jersey Air Pollution Control Act. “This enforcement action – by far the largest ever taken against a data center in New Jersey and possibly one of the largest such actions in the nation – sends a clear message that these facilities will not be constructed or operated with impunity in this state,” said DEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak.

item.title: Florida OIR Approves Four More HO Rate Cuts as Citizens Keeps Shrinking
item.description: And more rate cuts are on the way—further evidence that taking excessive litigation out of the equation has had a big impact on the once-struggling Florida property insurance market. Florida’s insurance commissioner announced his office has approved four rate decreases on homeowner policies, averaging 7% and affecting 62,000 policies at renewal. “I expect to see more aggressive rate cuts in the near future and going into 2027,” Commissioner Michael Yaworsky said in a statement Tuesday.

item.title: NAMIC, Xceedance Launch Virtual Estimating
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) The National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies (NAMIC; Indianapolis) and Xceedance (Fort Lauderdale, Fla.) have launched the NAMIC Virtual Estimating Program Powered by Xceedance. “The Virtual Estimating Program offers NAMIC members the best of both state-of-the-art AI technology and valuable human expertise for a more accurate and efficient claims process.” AI-Enabled Estimating The program uses AI-enabled technology to support scope development, repair identification, documentation review and quality checks. The NAMIC-endorsed program is designed to help mutual insurers improve estimate quality, reduce turnaround times and expand estimating capacity across residential property, auto physical damage and farm equipment claims, according to a joint statement.

item.title: NHTSA Closes Rear-View Camera Probe into 129,000 Honda Vehicles
item.description: auto safety regulator on Tuesday closed an investigation into rear-view camera failures in 129,092 Honda Ridgeline pickup trucks, recalled in 2022, without further action. The agency said most reports it received involved other rear-view camera or wire-harness failure modes and could not be linked to the durability issue under investigation. The work found no rear-view camera failures caused by wire-harness damage, the agency said, and indicated that the part was not expected to fail during a reasonable vehicle lifespan.

item.title: Ex-Google Safety Chief Warns AI Could Harm Children More Than Social Media Did
item.description: The founder of the trust and safety team at Alphabet’s Google this week called for a slowdown in AI development, warning that the tech industry was repeating the same mistakes from the social media era, potentially causing even greater harm to children. “The idea that the industry will figure it out by itself without outside help is unrealistic.” Siegel’s concerns mirror a growing fear among some tech insiders and academic researchers that AI poses a deeper threat to children than social media did, at a time when the industry is racing to add increasingly advanced features to chatbots that millions of young people already use daily. Social media companies are paying huge sums and facing thousands of lawsuits over claims they harmed young users, while governments around the world are working to curb minors’ access to their platforms.

item.description: The approach would follow recent revisions to the Justice Department’s guidelines related to the False Claims Act. Justice Department has encouraged prosecutors to dismiss more lawsuits against companies brought by whistleblowers, and the former top deputy for the agency’s civil division expects the trend to continue.

item.title: 60% expect property cat rates to fall, 86% expect T&Cs to loosen: Fitch reinsurance survey
item.description: Reinsurance companies are set to enter renewal negotiations from a position of capital strength, but the majority are expecting a challenging outcome, with prices expected to fall and terms and conditions expected to loosen further, a survey by Fitch Ratings found. In a survey carried out during the annual Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, Fitch Ratings found that reinsurance market conditions are driving underwriters to reduce their focus on property and property catastrophe risks, with fewer than 10% of respondents to its survey highlighting those lines of business as a high-priority for capital allocation. But, despite the fact reinsurers are saying their focus is elsewhere, conditions aren’t changing according to Fitch, who said that as capital supply continues to outpace demand for reinsurance protection the rating agency believes, “this factor will extend the buyer-friendly P&C market conditions, and increase pressure on reinsurers to achieve the best risk-adjusted returns with the lowest capital intensity.” 58% of respondents said that they expect terms and conditions will loosen selectively at the reinsurance renewals in 2027, with a further 28% saying they expect terms and conditions will loosen broadly and just 14% said T&Cs are expected to remain unchanged.

item.title: Direct institutional investor allocations to reinsurance grew at fastest rate in 2025: Marsh Re
item.description: Allocations to reinsurance grew fastest among direct institutional investors in 2025, outpacing the growth rate of assets deployed at independent insurance-linked securities managers and reinsurer sponsored managers, according to recent data from broker Marsh Re. But new information shared by Marsh Re shows that the growth rate has been different across the various cohorts of investor capital sources, with direct institutional investors growing their allocations to reinsurance at the fastest rate through 2025. Since 2013, when Marsh Re’s chart begins, the direct institutional investor bracket of allocators to reinsurance had been growing particularly slowly, but 2025 saw a meaningful uptick as it grew from $7 billion to $11 billion of the total third-party capital market.

item.title: Marsh and WEF call for place-based resilience to support insurability and reinsurance capacity
item.description: Marsh, a global insurance broking and risk management firm, and the World Economic Forum, an international organisation focused on public-private cooperation, are calling for greater investment in place-based resilience to support insurance and reinsurance availability and affordability as climate-related losses increase. The playbook, Addressing Insurability: A Playbook for Investing in Place-Based Resilience, says that conventional approaches often focus on protecting individual buildings or assets, while many of the risks affecting insurers and reinsurers extend beyond a single property. The organisations also distinguish between asset-level resilience and place-based resilience.

item.title: VIG expands telematics offering in CEE with Dolphin Technologies stake acquisition
item.description: Vienna Insurance Group (VIG), an Austria-based insurance group operating across Central and Eastern Europe (CEE), has acquired a 25% stake in Dolphin Technologies, a Vienna-based technology company. Founded in Vienna in 2001, Dolphin Technologies develops AI-powered telematics platforms and digital mobility services for insurance and automotive companies. Partnering with Dolphin enables VIG to continue broadening its market leadership in CEE telematics solutions, the firm stated.

item.title: RAA names John Bender as Chairman and Christopher Donelan as Vice Chairman
item.description: The Reinsurance Association of America (RAA), a US trade association representing companies operating in the reinsurance sector, has announced changes to its board leadership, with John Bender appointed Chairman and Christopher Donelan named Vice Chairman. Donelan, Chief Executive Officer of Global Reinsurance at Sompo International Holdings Ltd., becomes Vice Chairman. Bender, who is Chairman of Reinsurance and Risk Management at Allied World Assurance Company, takes over as chair of the RAA Board of Directors.
